title: Summer jobs: reading an email about working at children's summer camps
summary: A reading comprehension task based on an email from Hamed to Basim proposing a summer job at special-needs children's camps in the USA, with a multiple-choice question about Hamed's purpose for writing.

title: Focus on careers – conference interpreter: preparation, skills and qualifications
summary: A paired discussion activity followed by a reading text about Samira's career as a conference interpreter, covering her preparation, qualifications, working style and daily skills required for the job.

title: Unit 3 Revision: conditionals, reported questions and past regrets
summary: A revision page with sample sentences covering zero and first conditional, second conditional, reported questions, I wish and If only structures, and third conditional for discussing past regrets and unreal past situations.

title: Table of contents for Unit 4 listing the lesson topics
summary: A brief contents page listing the four main lesson topics of Unit 4: Rashid and Rana Designs, working out at home, how to be the best, and If only regrets.

title: My new business: email about setting up a clothing design company
summary: A gap-fill exercise where students complete an email about starting a shirt and jeans company called Rashid & Rana Designs, covering export success, London Fashion Week and signing contracts with department stores.

title: People didn't use to work out at home: fitness technology and home gyms
summary: An article about how new technologies and fitness apps have made home workouts more accessible, discussing online exercise communities and the growing competition gym owners now face.

title: How to be the best! matching advice for success in various situations
summary: Exercises where students match sentence halves giving advice on having a successful restaurant, making a good impression at interviews, running a business and other scenarios, then pair them with pictures.

title: If only: reading about regrets and practising I wish with third conditional
summary: Students read about three people with regrets—a football captain, a job interviewee and a motorbike rider—then match statements and practise making I wish and third conditional sentences from guiding questions.
